What made it survivable was that the men refusing orders were bargaining rather than breaking, and a bargain requires the other side to offer something. An army given nothing does not return to the condition it was in before it asked. It holds, less each month, until it is asked to do something it will not do at a moment when the enemy is watching.The front · 1 June 1918Expand the mapSoissonsParisVitry-le-FrancoisBar-sur-AubeChatillon-sur-SeineChantillyVerdunCalaisChemin des DamesLa MalmaisonDuryDoullensProvinsVillers-CotteretsCompiegne-9MANPOWER ▾-8MUNITIONS ▾-7ARMY MORALE ▾Speculative counterfactualSpeculative. The historical army recovered inside six weeks. Most accounts credit the pairing — leave, rest, and the promise, alongside a repression deliberately kept narrow. Removing half of that pairing is the counterfactual, and the evidence points where this ending points. What actually happened: The army recovered in weeks. Petain stopped the offensives, gave the men regular leave and better food, visited the divisions himself and listened to the grievances, and the courts-martial of the summer handed down several hundred death sentences, of which a few dozen were carried out.
